newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI Australia says to buy Indonesian plant.
newsitem.headline: ICI Australia says to buy Indonesian plant.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd said on Friday it had signed a heads of agreement for the purchase of an adhesives and resins plant in Indonesia for an undisclosed sum.

"We have signed the heads of agreement for the acquisition of an adhesives and resins business in Indonesia, which will be completed sometime in the early part of 1997," managing director Warren Haynes told a news conference.
Haynes said the plant would cost between A$10 million and A$50 million but declined to be more specific.
He also declined to identify the vendor.
The three-year-old plant produces raw materials used in the production of medium-density fibreboard.
"The medium density fibreboard business in Indonesia is really just getting underway. We believe it's going to be a growing market in Indonesia," Haynes said.
The fibreboard is used as a substitute for plywoods made from whole logs, which are in diminishing supply in Indonesia.
Haynes said ICI would invest in upgrading safety, health and environment standards to the company's benchmark levels.
